observed.description:
Observed is the statistic in the units a human recognises — for a ratio
that is the point estimate, not the confidence bound the comparison was
actually made against. Score carries the bound, or the robust z.

opened_outcomes.description:
The outcomes that opened it, frozen. A watch can be retuned mid-incident,
and a page that recomputed its own trigger would describe something that
never happened.

until.description:
Until is when the mute lifts. Null lifts it now, which is how somebody
un-mutes without having to pick a time in the past.

alerts_days.description:
AlertsDays is a pointer on the same terms as the other two, and for a
sharper reason: this axis has a non-zero default, so an omitted field
decoding to zero would silently switch alert-history pruning off — the
direction that grows a table nobody is looking at.

values.description:
Nullable: an entry is null where the scrape did not report that series,
which is a gap rather than a measurement of zero. A generated client that
types these as plain numbers will reject the first gap it meets.

Said here rather than declared in the schema because swaggo cannot mark an
array's items nullable — x-nullable lands on the array, which would claim
the column itself may be null, and that is a different and untrue thing.

truncated.description:
Truncated says the trace held more records than one response carries. It is
reported rather than silently applied, because a waterfall drawn from a cut
record set is wrong in a way nothing in the picture reveals.

conditions.description:
Conditions and Actions travel as the open objects they are stored as,
parameters and all.

Deliberately untyped here rather than a struct per kind: describing them
field by field would mean this package knowing every condition's
parameters, which is the one thing a discriminated shape exists to avoid,
and it would put a second definition of them beside the one the domain
already decodes strictly. The domain's own builder is what refuses a
malformed one, and it does so with a message naming the field.

attrs.description:
Attrs is whatever the runtime attached to the log call, passed through as it
sent it. swaggertype keeps the description honest about that: bytes to Go,
arbitrary JSON to a client.

cost_usd.description:
CostUSD is what could be priced and UnpricedCalls how many calls could not
be. They are reported side by side because the total alone is a lower bound
whenever the second is non-zero, and a reader with only the first has no way
to know that.

dropped_records.description:
DroppedRecords is how many records the publisher admitted losing in this
window. It is per app and never per trace: the marker carries no trace id,
so nothing can say which traces are incomplete — only that some are.

integration_id.description: IntegrationID is empty when the deployment could not be resolved to one.

deployment_ids.description:
DeploymentIDs is every deployment that contributed records. More than one
means the trace crossed apps: the id rides on the message and survives a
queue hop, so this is how a reader learns the trace is not one app's story.

body.description:
Body and Vars are null when the runtime captured no payload AND when the
caller asked for the trace without them. The two are indistinguishable here
by design: a client that asked for no bodies knows it did.
swaggertype says what RawMessage means on the wire: bytes to Go, arbitrary
JSON to a client. Without it the description would call these base64 strings.
Their shape belongs to the block that was traced, not to this API.

cache_write_tokens.description:
CacheWriteTokens is cache creation, billed above the input rate. NULL only
when the record carried no usage at all (including every record written
before the column existed); 0 when a provider reported usage but no write
count, which is every provider but Anthropic.

dropped.description:
Dropped marks a record the runtime shipped as incomplete; Truncated marks
one whose payload was cut to fit.

emptyAcquireCount.description:
EmptyAcquireCount is how often a caller had to wait for a connection, which
is the number that turns "the platform feels slow" into "the pool is too
small".

keyspaceHits.description:
Hits and Misses are cumulative since the server started. The ratio is what
anyone actually reads, but both are reported because a high ratio over a tiny
sample says nothing.

maxMemoryBytes.description:
MaxMemory 0 means no ceiling is configured, which is worth showing as such
rather than as a usage of 100% or of 0%.

redisReason.description:
RedisReason and DatabaseReason say why a half is absent, so the page can tell
"this installation has no Redis" from "Redis is down".

info.description:
The platform's observability surface: stored log events and traces as
shipped by deployed runtimes, the pod stats the stats sidecar collects,
the retention policy over what is kept, and a report on how full the
two stores underneath are.

This is an in-cluster service and performs no authentication of its own.
It is ClusterIP in the chart and the platform BFF is the authorization
boundary in front of it. Every query route is a read; the three
retention routes are the exception, and one of them deletes stored
telemetry — so anything that can reach this address can erase it as
well as read it. Keep it internal.
info.title: Octo Observability API

get.description:
The same rows as a single watch's history, across every watch — the view that
answers "what has alerting been doing" rather than "what has this watch been
doing". Paged on an opaque cursor naming an (evaluated_at, id) pair, because a
tick evaluates every due watch inside the same millisecond.

parameters.description: Only rows belonging to this episode
parameters.name: incidentId

parameters.description: Opaque cursor from a previous page's next_before
parameters.name: before

get.description:
Firing episodes, most recent first. `open=true` is the "what is on fire right
now" view. A closed episode carries the reason it closed, and "resolved" is
deliberately distinct from "stale": the second means the watch stopped being
able to decide, which is not the same as the metric coming back.

parameters.description: Only episodes that are still running
parameters.name: open

parameters.description: RFC3339 lower bound on when it opened
parameters.name: from

post.description:
Records that somebody has seen it. It does not resolve the episode — only the
metric coming back does that — and acknowledging one twice is refused rather
than silently re-stamping whoever got there first.

Runs the definition against real data now and reports what each condition
observed, what it was judged against, and whether it held — without recording
an evaluation, moving any state or notifying anybody. It takes a whole watch
rather than an id, because the question is worth asking about a definition
that has not been saved: it is how a spike's gates get tuned before the watch
goes live rather than after it fails to fire.

get.description:
Every watch, newest first, each with where its state machine has got to —
the phase it is in, when it last ran, and the incident it currently holds
open. A watch whose stored definition this service cannot read comes back
with phase "invalid" rather than being omitted.

post.description:
Validates the whole definition before storing it: every condition is built,
every action is checked, and an unrecognised condition or action type is
refused rather than stored to fail at three in the morning. The watch is due
on the next tick.

400.description: the definition is not one this service can evaluate

409.description: the name is taken, or this installation is at its limit

delete.description:
Closes any open episode first, then removes the watch and everything that
referenced it — its state, its incidents and its evaluation history. An
incident that outlived its watch would have nothing left that could resolve it.

put.description:
A save replaces the whole definition. Retuning anything that changes what a
pending hold means — a condition, the combinator, the hold itself — restarts
that hold on the next evaluation, because the clock was measuring a different
question. Renaming a watch or changing its recipients does not. Disabling one
closes any episode it has open.

get.description:
Every time this watch was asked, newest first — including the ticks that found
nothing, which is what makes "it was evaluated and it was fine" distinguishable
from "it was never evaluated". `notable=true` drops the quiet rows.

parameters.description: Only rows belonging to this episode
parameters.name: incidentId

parameters.description: Opaque cursor from a previous page's next_before
parameters.name: before

post.description:
Suppresses notifications until the given time without stopping evaluation, so
the history stays complete and an open incident still resolves on its own. A
null `until` lifts the mute. Silencing a watch permanently is what `enabled`
is for, so a mute may not be set more than 30 days ahead.

get.description:
Answers as soon as the process is serving, whether or not Postgres or
NATS are reachable — it is what the readiness probe polls while the
rest is still coming up.

One page of stored log events, newest first. Every filter is optional and
they combine; a page that came back full carries next_before, which is the
cursor to send as before= for the page after it.

parameters.description: Only these levels; repeat the parameter for more than one
parameters.name: level

parameters.description: A previous page's next_before. Opaque — it names a (ts, id) pair, not a timestamp
parameters.name: before

400.description: a time is not RFC3339, the cursor is malformed, or limit is not a number

get.description:
This API as an OpenAPI 3.1 document. Narrow it with tag or path — the
full document is mostly schemas, and a filtered one carries only the
schemas its operations can reach. The two filters are alternatives, not
a combination.

parameters.description: Keep only operations carrying this tag
parameters.name: tag

parameters.description: Keep only routes starting with this prefix
parameters.name: path

400.description: tag and path were both supplied

get.description:
Every route as one line: method, path, summary and tags. Read this
first to find the tag or path worth asking the description about.

post.description:
Deletes what the stored policy no longer keeps and reports how much went.
This is what the chart's nightly job calls. A policy that keeps everything
is a 200 with zero counts and null cutoffs rather than an error — being
asked to do nothing is an answer.

A trace is deleted whole: its records go with its summary, so a swept trace
never becomes one that lists but cannot be opened. Stored model prices are
never swept, because a traced call's cost points into that history.

get.description:
How many days of log events, of traces, and of alerting history this
installation keeps. Zero on an axis means keep forever. Logs and traces
default to zero; the alerting history defaults to 14 days, because an
evaluation log is diagnostic rather than evidence and its volume does not
depend on anything happening.

put.description:
All three windows are supplied on every save. Zero keeps that stream
forever; the maximum is 3650 days. Saving does not delete anything — the
sweep runs nightly, or on demand through POST /retention/run.

oneOf.description: The three retention windows, in days. All are required

requestBody.description: The three retention windows, in days. All are required

400.description: a window is missing, negative, or beyond 3650 days

get.description:
Memory against the ceiling, hit rate and evictions for Redis; this
service's connection pool usage and the size of the object store's
table for Postgres. Either half is null when this installation does
not have that store or cannot reach it, with the reason alongside — an
installation with no Redis is supported, and is not the same as one
whose Redis is down.
get.summary: How full the platform's two stores are

get.description:
The catalogue, built from the pods' dictionaries alone — no samples are read.
It exists so a caller can find exact metric names before asking for data,
which is what makes the required metric filter on the series route usable.

Label sets are nested under their metric name. One histogram is a single
entry with a series per bucket boundary, rather than a hundred names that
happen to share a prefix.

truncated means the pod list hit its cap, so the catalogue is partial: a
metric missing from it may simply belong to a pod that was dropped.

parameters.description: Only these pods; repeat the parameter for more than one
parameters.name: pod

parameters.description: Only metrics whose name starts with this
parameters.name: prefix

get.summary: List the metrics a deployment exposes

get.description:
Every pod of the deployment the stats index still holds, most recently seen
first. Read this first: it names the pods the other two routes accept, and
says whether each is still reporting.

liveRows and rollupRows are reported separately on purpose. Zero live rows
beside a full history is the ordinary state of a pod that stopped a few hours
ago, because the live tier is kept for only twice the rollup interval while
the pod stays in the index for the whole retention window.

An unknown deployment answers 200 with no items rather than 404. This service
holds no deployment registry, so it cannot tell a deployment that never
existed from one whose sidecar is switched off or whose stats have expired.
get.summary: List the pods reporting stats for a deployment

get.description:
Points for the named metrics, per pod, decoded against each pod's dictionary.

metric is required, and repeatable. It is what bounds the response: the rows
are stored positionally, so a query with no name filter would read every
series of every pod. Use the metrics route to find the names.

A counter's value is its growth over the interval ending at that point, on
both tiers, so a chart does not have to know which tier answered. Its closing
cumulative reading is available as the last stat on the rollup tier, and
counters=absolute returns the raw readings instead. A counter that went
backwards is treated as a process restart rather than a negative delta.

tier=auto picks live when the window fits inside the live tier's reach and
rollup otherwise, because a window older than that cannot be answered from
live rows however many are read. The resolved tier and its step are echoed
back.

times are unix milliseconds, oldest first, and the columns are parallel. A
null value is a gap rather than a zero. On the rollup tier ends is carried
too, because rows are not contiguous: when a bucket's end does not meet the
next one's start, scraping had stopped in between.

parameters.description: Metric names, matched exactly; repeat the parameter for more than one
parameters.name: metric

parameters.description: Narrow within those metrics, as key=value; repeated labels are ANDed
parameters.name: label

parameters.description: Only these pods; repeat the parameter for more than one
parameters.name: pod

parameters.description: Start of the window, RFC3339. Defaults to 15 minutes before to
parameters.name: from

parameters.description: End of the window, RFC3339. Defaults to now
parameters.name: to

parameters.description: Which numbers to return, comma separated: value, min, max, last, samples. Rollup tier only
parameters.name: stats

parameters.description: delta for growth, absolute for the raw cumulative reading
parameters.name: counters

400.description: no metric was named, a time is not RFC3339, or a parameter is not one of its values

get.summary: Read stats series for a deployment

get.description:
One page of trace summaries, newest first. Every filter is optional and they
combine; a page that came back full carries next_before, which is the cursor
to send as before= for the page after it.

Unlike /traces/apps neither time bound is defaulted, so an unfiltered call
reaches back as far as the store goes.

parameters.description: Only this deployment's traces; must be a uuid
parameters.name: deploymentId

parameters.description: Only this integration's traces; must be a uuid
parameters.name: integrationId

parameters.description: Only traces whose root flow is this one
parameters.name: flow

parameters.description: Only these outcomes; repeat the parameter for more than one
parameters.name: status

parameters.description: Pass true for only the traces that called a model
parameters.name: hasLlm

parameters.description: Only traces at least this long, in milliseconds
parameters.name: minDurationMs

parameters.description: A previous page's next_before. Opaque — it names a (started_at, trace_id) pair
parameters.name: before

400.description: an id is not a uuid, a status is not one of ok/dropped/failed, a time is not RFC3339, to is before from, or a number is malformed

get.description:
Every app that ran a trace in the window, with its counts and cost. Read this
first to find the app worth listing traces for.

The window is echoed back in the response, because the caller may not have
chosen it and every count is meaningless without it. Either bound may be given
alone: from with no to reads to now, and to with no from reads back 24 hours.

parameters.description: Start of the window, RFC3339. Defaults to 24h before to
parameters.name: from

parameters.description: End of the window, RFC3339. Defaults to now
parameters.name: to

400.description: a time is not RFC3339, or to is before from

get.description:
One trace: the summary the list already showed, plus every record that fed
it, in sequence. The summary is the stored rollup rather than a recomputation,
so the number here and the number in the list are the same number.

Captured payloads are the whole weight of a trace. A client drawing only a
waterfall should pass bodies=0 and leave them on the server, then fetch the one
record it needs from /traces/{traceId}/records/{id}.

parameters.description: Pass 0 or false to omit the captured payloads. Defaults to including them
parameters.name: bodies

get.description:
One record with its captured payloads, for a client that loaded the trace
with bodies=0 and then opened a single block.

A malformed id answers 404 rather than 400: it addresses no record either
way, and answering alike for "malformed" and "absent" keeps the route from
confirming which ids exist.

404.description: no such record, or the id is not a uuid
